analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+Serve.swift head 429-432: the control-event reader now calls noteCoordinatorRequest() when an inferenceRequest arrives, then still yields it to the work FIFO. noteCoordinatorRequest (ServingAuthorizationRecovery head patch) only stamps coordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt when the connection is connected. It is a local diagnostic/recovery timestamp. It does not touch decryption, admission or authorization. Coordinator-side routing authorization (TB-011, T-053, A-016) remains authoritative, and clearConnectionAuthorization on connect/disconnect is unchanged.

superviseServingAuthorization now dispatches on ServingReadiness.verdict(connection:trust:now:) instead of UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.connectionLacksAuthorization. Under the new mapping:
- blocked with advertised models leads to superviseRefusedConnection, which keeps the shouldReconnect throttle and the idle check.
- authorized resets the reconnect attempts.
- pending, unconfirmed or nil clears unauthorizedSince.

This governs only self-initiated re-registration and logging (an availability concern, A-018). Serving permission is unaffected. A coordinator-routed request supersedes earlier refusal evidence. Only the trusted coordinator can produce that request, so there is no adversary-controlled trigger. A consumer cannot forge an inferenceRequest on the provider socket.

Unverified: ServingReadiness.verdict's source is not supplied. Integration should confirm two points:
- verdict does not treat lastRequestAt as authorization for any admission decision.
- The base semantics are preserved, i.e. the old resetting of reconnect attempts on a current App Attest grant or the legacy path now happens through the .authorized case.

If verdict can return pending/unconfirmed indefinitely for a refused connection, that would be an availability-only weakening of recovery, not a security regression. No change to T-041, the cache scope plumbing, or the attestation/registration code at head 540-622.
